    Fit simplified epidemic models with data-first column selection

    Source: R/fit-data-first.R
    epi_fit_renewal.Rd

    Data-first alternatives to the formula-based engine functions used by parsnip. The renewal fit estimates a constant reproduction number using a conditional Poisson mean and fixed generation weights. The compartmental fit estimates transmission by least squares with the population, recovery and initial states fixed. These methods use the same models and assumptions as epi_renewal() and epi_compartmental(); this is not a calibrated or validated forecasting system. Select exactly one distinct column for each argument; non-syntactic names can be selected using backticks or all_of().

    Usage

    epi_fit_renewal(.data, time, cases, weights = 1)

epi_fit_compartmental(
  .data,
  time,
  infectious,
  population,
  gamma,
  beta_max = 10,
  model = c("sir", "seir"),
  sigma = NULL,
  initial_exposed = 0,
  initial_recovered = 0
)

    Arguments

    .data

    An ungrouped data frame with consecutive integer time steps.

    time

    A single time column selected using tidy selection.

    cases

    A single non-negative integer incidence column for renewal.

    weights

    Generation-interval probabilities by lag, summing to one.

    infectious

    A single non-negative infectious prevalence column for the compartmental fit. The first value supplies the initial infectious count.

    population

    Fixed total population greater than initial compartments.

    gamma

    Fixed non-negative recovery rate.

    beta_max

    Positive upper bound for transmission-rate optimization.

    model

    Either "sir" or "seir".

    sigma

    Fixed positive progression rate, required for SEIR.

    initial_exposed

    Fixed non-negative initial exposed count, zero for SIR.

    initial_recovered

    Fixed non-negative initial recovered count.

    Value

    A fitted epi_model suitable for predict(), generics::tidy(), generics::glance() and generics::augment(). This is an engine model, not a parsnip model specification.

    Examples

    d <- data.frame(day = 1:5, cases = c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16))
fit <- epi_fit_renewal(d, day, cases, weights = 1)
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(day = 6:7))
#> [1] 32 64
c <- data.frame(day = 0:4, infectious = c(5, 6, 7, 8, 9))
epi_fit_compartmental(c, day, infectious, population = 1000, gamma = .1)
#> $kind
#> [1] "compartmental"
#> 
#> $model
#> [1] "sir"
#> 
#> $estimate
#> [1] 0.2612765
#> 
#> $gamma
#> [1] 0.1
#> 
#> $sigma
#> NULL
#> 
#> $initial_exposed
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $initial_recovered
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $population
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $time
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4
#> 
#> $outcome_name
#> [1] "infectious"
#> 
#> $time_name
#> [1] "day"
#> 
#> $observed
#> [1] 5 6 7 8 9
#> 
#> $fitted
#> [1] 5.000000 5.823189 6.779768 7.890592 9.179504
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "epi_model"
